
Forge did not edit any existing file. Wire the resource by hand:

  1. Declare the new modules (each in the listed file, keeping `mod` lines sorted):

       src/domain/entities/mod.rs             pub mod tag;
       src/application/ports/mod.rs           pub mod tag_repository;
       src/application/use_cases/mod.rs       pub mod tags;
       src/infrastructure/database/mod.rs     pub mod tags;
       src/adapters/http/mod.rs               pub mod api_access;
       src/adapters/http/mod.rs               pub mod tags_api;

  2. In src/bootstrap/mod.rs, at the end of `fn compose`, before `Ok(())`:

    let tags = crate::application::use_cases::tags::TagService::new(std::sync::Arc::new(
        crate::infrastructure::database::tags::MySqlTagRepository::new(
            composition.mysql()?.clone(),
        ),
    ));
    // tags JSON API (/v1/tags): global. DenyAll refuses every request until
    // you decide who may use it: implement ApiGlobalAccess
    // (src/adapters/http/api_access.rs).
    crate::adapters::http::tags_api::routes(
        composition.router(),
        tags,
        std::sync::Arc::new(crate::adapters::http::api_access::DenyAll),
    )?;

  Every route of /v1/tags asks the access policy for `tags:read` or
  `tags:write` first; src/adapters/http/api_access.rs explains the
  deny-by-default choice.

  Then apply the migration (`cargo run -- migrate` with FORGE_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL)
  and run `cargo test` (repository tests on a database server need
  `cargo test -- --include-ignored` and FORGE_TEST_* URLs, see docs/database.md).
